title: Anthropic raises misalignment risk to 'low' in August risk report, discloses internal Model 2
subtitle: The company's second Responsible Scaling Policy risk report bumps its estimate up one notch and reveals an unreleased frontier system more capable than Mythos 5.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic published its August 2026 Risk Report on August 15, the second such disclosure under version 3.4 of its Responsible Scaling Policy and the first since February. The company raised its estimate of catastrophic-misalignment risk in high-stakes settings from 'very low' to 'low,' and disclosed an internal frontier model it calls Model 2 — described as noticeably more capable than the released Mythos 5, but not scheduled for external release.

The label change is not a claim that misalignment actually got worse. Anthropic writes that the shift is driven by rising uncertainty — several safety benchmarks the company relied on in February have started to saturate, and recent cyber-evaluation incidents (including the OpenAI Hugging Face breach and its own Claude cyber-test disclosures) have widened the error bars on what a frontier system can do without human oversight. When you can no longer distinguish 'very safe' from 'safe' with your instruments, honest reporting is to say so.

Model 2 is the more consequential detail. Anthropic has now confirmed publicly that its strongest internal system is a step beyond Mythos 5, has not been through the full predeployment safety suite, and is being held back from external release. This is the pattern the Responsible Scaling Policy is supposed to produce — build the model, evaluate it, then decide whether the world gets it — and this is the first time a frontier lab has said, in a formal risk document, that a completed model is staying inside. It sets a precedent other labs will now be asked about.

A takeaway for learners: the language of risk reports rewards patience. 'Low' and 'very low' sound close, but Anthropic's own explanation is that the change reflects instrument limits, not model behavior. If you plan to work in AI safety or policy, learn to read these documents for what they measure and what they can no longer measure — the gap between the two is where the interesting work is.
